name: DonnyFest
size: Free day festival, plays to thousands
asks: Spotify profile, a live video if you have one, social links and a short bio
read: Built for emerging and local acts, with a lean towards Yorkshire. They only ask for Spotify and a live clip, so you can apply as you are.

name: Home Farm Festival
read: The window is four weeks and they say it may close early if they get too many applications. Apply on the day it opens.

name: Teddy Rocks
asks: One music link (SoundCloud, Bandcamp or YouTube), up to 3 genres and a pitch of up to 280 characters
deadline: Rolling; reviewed close to the festival
read: A rock-first lineup and a short form. Put your effort into the 280-character pitch. It's in spring, so it works as a warm-up for summer.

name: Loopfest
asks: Online form; asks whether any member is under 18
read: Every venue has a PA, a sound tech, amps and a basic three-piece kit, so it costs very little to play. Good live practice before summer.

name: Dart Music Festival
pay: Negotiated fee you propose; no travel or accommodation
asks: Music links (live recordings encouraged), public liability insurance, PRS details, proposed fee, available all 3 days
read: One of the few that pays. Price in your fuel. No backline is provided, and only two venues have a drum kit.

name: Twyfest
pay: Unpaid (stage, sound, lights and some drinks)
asks: A link to your music and a few words about you, emailed to bands@twyfest.uk
read: The easiest yes on this list if Berkshire is within reach. Local acts get priority.

name: Wokingham Festival
size: Two stages: main stage and marquee
read: Books emerging local acts alongside established ones. They don't reply to everyone.

name: Music Barn
asks: Your bio and a link to your music, through their contact form
read: They say they listen to every submission and book as many acts as they can. One of the most open doors on the list.

name: Exeter Respect
asks: A YouTube performance video, a 50-word description, your tech spec and two landscape photos (1920 × 1080 or bigger)
read: A community festival with its 2027 form already live. The photo and video requirements mean your press kit needs to be ready first.

name: Rattler Fest, Great Estate and Little Orchard
size: Three small festivals run by one promoter
asks: One form for all three: act name, location, genre and a bio
read: One application puts you in front of three Cornish festivals. Send it once only; they treat repeat entries as spam.

name: Eskfest
read: A simple email application with a clear deadline. Send your live video and Spotify link.

name: Dot to Dot
asks: Google Form linked from their information page
read: The best genre fit on the list: it's an indie and alt festival. Most acts on the bill have a team behind them, but anyone can use the form.

name: Camper Calling
read: The Freshly Squeezed stage is for BBC Introducing acts, so upload to BBC Introducing before you apply.

name: Sunshine Festival
asks: Links to performances (required), genre and experience, and which days Thu–Sun you're free
read: Open to anyone, but thousands apply and they won't consider entries without links to live performances. Send a live video, not just Spotify.

name: Together Again
read: Run by Escape Records. The form is live, but the page says very little about who they book.

name: FOCUS Wales
size: Showcase: about 100 open slots, 250+ artists in total, 20 stages, music industry attending
asks: Free Amplead application or Google Form; no covers or tribute acts; 30-minute sets
read: A showcase that music industry people attend. It's free, open to all genres and takes artists from anywhere, which is rare for a European showcase.

name: Meadow Fest
read: Listed as open by ICMP. There's little detail, so it costs you nothing but a message.

name: Tramlines Apply to Play
size: Large city festival with a dedicated emerging-artist scheme
pay: Paid slots for finalists. The winner also gets paid slots at Truck, Y Not and Victorious
asks: Online application; a shortlist then goes to a judging panel and a public vote
deadline: Not open yet; last year's closed 28 Jan
read: Open to emerging and unsigned artists across the UK, and it has won Best Festival for Emerging Talent. One win gets you onto four festivals. Watch for it opening around December.

name: Victorious Apply to Play
deadline: Not open yet; last year's ran 7 Nov to 28 Mar
read: Only for emerging artists with a PO postcode, but if that's you, the odds are good: over 2,000 slots have gone to local acts since 2017.

name: Deer Shed Apply to Play
pay: A paid slot, plus mentoring from EMI North
deadline: Not open yet; last year's closed 2 Apr
read: Only for artists based in Yorkshire, the North East, the North West or Scotland. Run with EMI North, so you get label mentoring as well as the slot.

name: Truck Band App
size: Mid-size indie festival, 25+ slots for local acts
pay: Paid slots across the main stages
asks: Application, then a shortlist judged by local tastemakers, BBC Introducing Oxford and a public vote
read: Mainly for acts from around Oxford. Past picks include Cassia and Fur, so it's a real launchpad for indie bands.

name: Wychwood
read: They've confirmed 2027 artist applications will open later in the year. It ran an apply-to-play for 2026 too.

name: Liverpool Sound City
size: Multi-venue new-music showcase with industry attending
read: Crock Pot Cartel lists it as opening soon. Join their mailing list now so you hear the day the form goes live.

name: The Great Escape
read: The biggest new-music showcase in the UK. Most slots go to acts with a label, agent or PR. It's free, so apply. No reply by 31 March means no.

name: Glastonbury Emerging Talent Competition
size: Thousands enter, 90 make the longlist, 8 the final
pay: £5,000 PRS Foundation prize for the winner
asks: Last time: one original song plus a video of you playing live
read: Free to enter, and the live video you make now covers it. The winner plays a main stage.

name: End of the Road emerging artists
deadline: Not open yet; usually closes late January
read: Winners open one of the main stages and one films a session with The Line of Best Fit. Very competitive, but it's exactly your scene.

name: Wide Days
asks: Original music; acts must be based in Scotland
read: Only an option if you're based in Scotland. A showcase that music industry people attend, with a year-long mentoring programme for four acts.

name: 2000trees
read: The right scene for you, but the bill is booked through agents. A short, polite email with your live video is the most you can do.

name: Y Not?
read: Sign up to their newsletter so you hear when the form opens.

name: Kendal Calling
read: Indie-heavy bill, but booked through agents.

name: Green Man
read: Booked through agents. Its Green Man Rising competition is the usual way in for new bands; watch for it opening.

name: Camp Bestival
read: Family bill and booked through agents. Low fit.

name: ArcTanGent
read: Only a fit if your sound leans math or post-rock.

name: Boomtown
read: Their 2027 window closed in February 2026, over a year early. For 2028, look for it in January 2027.

name: Tewkesbury Live
pay: Venues cover much of the band costs
deadline: Closed; results by end of Feb 2027
read: A good fit for next year: rock, pop, punk, and the venues help with costs. Ask events@tewkesburytowncouncil.gov.uk when the 2028 window opens.
